inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,350 normalized lines. Atkinson converts the critical-line second moment into a shifted double-series problem, continues the shifted series by Poisson and divisor/Voronoi summation, decomposes the mean value into four oscillatory integrals, and uses a reusable complex saddle-point lemma to extract two finite oscillatory sums with controlled remainders. The prose supports this architecture, but many displayed formulas are OCR-damaged; units whose exact coefficients or phases depend on those displays are explicitly marked for scan verification.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Statement, divisor analogy, and proof overview
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Places the zeta second moment beside the divisor problem, states the two-family approximate formula, and outlines the shifted-series-to-saddle-point route.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Meromorphic continuation of the shifted series
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Separates the diagonal and off-diagonal double Dirichlet series and continues the latter after isolating polar terms.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Poisson representation and the critical product identity
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses Poisson summation to obtain a convergent divisor-weighted integral series and takes the exceptional limit u+v=1.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Voronoi continuation and mean-value decomposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Continues the boundary function with divisor summation, verifies convergence of its pieces, and rewrites the second moment as four integrals; the final explicit kernel display is extraction-defective.

sections_inspected.label: 5. General saddle-point lemma
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Proves a uniform contour-deformation estimate with a stationary contribution, endpoint terms, and analytic error control.

sections_inspected.label: 6. Logarithmic-phase specialization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Specializes the general saddle lemma to the phase and amplitude occurring in the four mean-value integrals.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Estimates of I1 and I2
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extracts the first finite oscillatory family and bounds the companion term.

sections_inspected.label: 8. Estimate of I3
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Splits small and large ranges and combines mean-value, saddle, and contour estimates to isolate the surviving constant contribution.

sections_inspected.label: 9. Reduction and saddle analysis of I4
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Evaluates the inner kernel, inserts the Voronoi expansion, and proves a second stationary-phase lemma with explicit existence conditions.

sections_inspected.label: 10. Completion of I4 and the theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Controls transition ranges by partial summation, obtains the second finite oscillatory family, and recombines all four integrals.

accepted_units.title: The zeta second moment as a divisor-problem analogue
accepted_units.why_material: The source identifies the structural target: refine the classical mean-value asymptotic in the way Voronoi refinement improves the divisor summatory formula, rather than merely sharpen an undifferentiated error term.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical formulas and claimed prior error exponents are partially degraded, but the analogy and research objective are explicit in prose.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the conceptual analogy; scan verification is needed for exact exponents and constants.

accepted_units.title: An approximate formula with two distinct oscillatory groups
accepted_units.why_material: The theorem organizes the mean-value remainder into two finite oscillatory families, one asymptotic to low-index Voronoi terms and another formally associated with the functional-equation product. This is the paper's central representational claim.
accepted_units.context_note: The parameter regime N comparable to T and the prose interpretation are legible; the displayed phases and amplitudes are not fully recoverable from OCR.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact formula reuse; verify the original scan before using coefficients, cutoffs, signs, or phases.

accepted_units.title: Classify off-diagonal pairs by their difference
accepted_units.why_material: Reindexing the product by m-n turns the mean-value problem into a shifted double series. Poisson summation, continuation by Voronoi summation, integration on the critical line, and saddle analysis then form a composable proof route.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is a prose-level map of later sections and supplies the semantic link among otherwise technical transformations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low; the mechanism is recoverable from prose despite damaged displayed identities.

accepted_units.title: Expose polar pieces before continuing the shifted series
accepted_units.why_material: Euler summation separates explicit zeta/polar contributions from a bounded-periodic remainder, showing how an initially convergent off-diagonal series becomes meromorphic in a larger region without conflating poles with the regular part.
accepted_units.context_note: The concluding regularity region and exceptional polar loci are legible; several intermediate formulas are damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; the continuation strategy is prose-supported, while exact normalizations require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation produces a divisor-weighted analytic continuation
accepted_units.why_material: Poisson summation converts the shift sum into cosine-transform integrals weighted by divisor-power sums, with an explicit uniform decay argument supporting absolute convergence and analytic continuation. Continuity then resolves the exceptional boundary u+v=1 in the zeta-product identity.
accepted_units.context_note: The convergence domains and continuity argument are readable; the limit formula has OCR loss in gamma factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium to high; the bridge is secure, but exact gamma and constant terms should be checked against the scan.

accepted_units.title: Continue the boundary function by splitting divisor summation into smooth and oscillatory parts
accepted_units.why_material: The source truncates the divisor-weighted kernel, applies the divisor summation formula D+J to the tail, and decomposes the continuation into four pieces with different analytic roles. This is the decisive bridge from the shifted series to Voronoi-type oscillation.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions of h and the four-way decomposition are identifiable, but the printed Voronoi expansion is significantly degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for exact kernels and constants; later use should reopen the scan, while the decomposition mechanism is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Use derivative decay and contour rearrangement to reach the critical boundary
accepted_units.why_material: Atkinson controls the derivative kernel against the divisor-error bound and rearranges the remaining oscillatory integrals to prove uniform convergence at the critical boundary. The move separates a formal continuation from an actually convergent boundary representation.
accepted_units.context_note: The endpoint conclusion is clear; several contour-integral displays and exponents are formula-unsafe in extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for quantitative bounds; scan verification is required before reproducing the estimates.

accepted_units.title: Convert the continued product identity into four mean-value integrals
accepted_units.why_material: Integrating the boundary identity and using Stirling isolates the classical main term and partitions the remaining contribution into I1-I4, assigning subsequent saddle and error analysis to distinct analytic components. The truncation parameter N is explicitly restricted to be comparable with T.
accepted_units.context_note: The high-level decomposition and N-range are legible, although individual integral displays are damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium; structural decomposition is reliable, exact integral formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A uniform complex saddle-point estimate with endpoint control
accepted_units.why_material: The lemma packages analyticity, local scale, curvature, and amplitude hypotheses into a stationary contribution plus endpoint and uniform error terms. Its proof deforms the contour through the saddle, obtains exponential decay away from it, and uses Gaussian symmetry to discard odd local terms.
accepted_units.context_note: Hypotheses and proof logic are readable; the compact displayed error formula and some Taylor exponents are degraded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium to high; conceptual use is supported, but exact error exponents must be checked from the scan.

accepted_units.title: Specialize the saddle lemma to the logarithmic mean-value phase
accepted_units.why_material: The specialization solves the stationary equation explicitly through variables U and V, separates positive and negative frequency behavior, and derives different remainder regimes for k below or above T. This turns a general contour lemma into the phase calculus used by the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The definitions of U and V, the stationary equation, and the regime split survive; the leading displayed integral formula is damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for amplitude, phase, and uniform-error details; original-page verification is necessary.

accepted_units.title: The first saddle contribution yields the Voronoi-like oscillatory family
accepted_units.why_material: Applying the specialized lemma uniformly and letting auxiliary integration limits tend to their endpoints produces the I1 finite oscillatory sum for N comparable with T, while I2 is reduced to a smaller divisor-error contribution.
accepted_units.context_note: The inference and I2 bound are readable, but the I1 displayed amplitude and phase are substantially corrupted.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; use the scan for the exact first-family formula.

accepted_units.title: Range splitting isolates the nonoscillatory contribution of I3
accepted_units.why_material: The source splits the kernel at its natural scale and again at y=1, using monotonicity plus the second mean-value theorem on the smallest range, the saddle lemma on the tail, and contour estimates on the remaining terms. The pieces combine to a constant contribution with a controlled error.
accepted_units.context_note: The sequence of estimates and final order are prose-supported; the exact constant display is OCR-ambiguous.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Medium to high; the method is reusable, but the final constant and intermediate kernels need scan confirmation.

accepted_units.title: Insert the Voronoi expansion after evaluating the I4 inner kernel
accepted_units.why_material: A first saddle estimate simplifies the inner kernel, after which the oscillatory divisor-error expansion is inserted and the variable is changed to produce a family of one-dimensional phase integrals J_n. This composes two asymptotic representations rather than attacking I4 directly.
accepted_units.context_note: The order estimates and transformation sequence are readable; the exact J_n phase and amplitude are damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; scan verification is required for the transformed integral.

accepted_units.title: A second saddle criterion selects when the dual phase contributes
accepted_units.why_material: The second lemma applies the general saddle machinery to J_n, records inequalities under which a stationary point exists, and omits the main term when the sign or index conditions fail. Thus the finite dual sum is selected by geometry of the phase rather than an arbitrary cutoff.
accepted_units.context_note: The qualitative conditions and no-saddle alternative are explicit, but several inequalities and the main-term display are OCR-damaged.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High; exact admissible range, phase, amplitude, and error must be verified against the source scan.

accepted_units.title: Transition-range estimates complete the second oscillatory family
accepted_units.why_material: After applying the second saddle lemma, Atkinson splits the residual divisor sums around the transition index, uses partial summation and the divisor asymptotic to control near and far ranges, replaces the cutoff by an equivalent explicit one, and recombines I1-I4 to prove the theorem.
accepted_units.context_note: The summation strategy and final recombination are clear; the exact cutoff and phase retain OCR damage.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High for the published final formula, medium for the transition-splitting mechanism.
